summary: The admitted pet crosses a LEVEL_TELEP trap, but the JS mlevel_tele_trap() still refused this C branch as non-hole monster level teleportation. Port the LEVEL_TELEP arm from teleport.c:mlevel_tele_trap(), including random destination selection, same-level shudder, migration type, visibility message, trap discovery, and teleport-control confusion. Pass the caller RNG into random_teleport_level() so preflight uses its cloned stream instead of advancing the live RNG.

source.branch: mlevel_tele_trap():2048-2072 handles LEVEL_TELEP and NO_TRAP after hole and portal cases. For LEVEL_TELEP it refuses amulet carriers/endgame monsters, calls random_teleport_level(), shudders if the destination depth is unchanged, otherwise calls get_level() and later migrates with MIGR_RANDOM. A visible monster disappears out of sight, reveals the trap, and becomes confused without teleport control.
callers: trap.c:dotrap() dispatches monster trap effects to teleport.c:mlevel_tele_trap(); js/trap_effects.js:trapeffect_selector() uses js/teleport.js:mlevel_tele_trap().
teleport.c:mlevel_tele_trap() calls random_teleport_level(); its JS caller passes the active RNG, including the cloned RNG used during elapsed-turn planning.
dependencies: teleport.c:random_teleport_level() and the caller-owned rn2/rnd stream
teleport.c:get_level() and dog.c:migrate_to_level() existing destination and migration helpers

evidence: The admitted v71 baseline evaluation at 62083786357189a4660adb0b96d92609e3d885b7 reports 329/415 screens, 2445/2480 RNG calls and 329/415 cursors before refusing step 329 with UnsupportedPositionCheckError: non-hole monster level teleportation. The v71 manifest SHA is f91e637b94dd4224eece47941f88a7f3a3e2d50eb31793ceddf2949b3ff3e703 and the case recording SHA is 29326f4f7c4f6db577334cf7947fef008902c3b23f89a6d60684ab3ebb2928ae.

Upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/teleport.c:2006-2086 shows mlevel_tele_trap() branch order: hole/trapdoor, portal, then LEVEL_TELEP/NO_TRAP. The new branch uses random_teleport_level(), calls get_level() only when destination depth changes, and continues through the shared visible disappearance, seetrap, confusion, and random migration tail.

The first post-port scan exposed a planning RNG leak: mlevel_tele_trap() reached random_teleport_level() in the cloned elapsed-turn plan, but that helper used module-global rn2/rnd. The level-teleporter caller now passes its RNG into random_teleport_level(), which preserves its existing default live stream for other callers.

The source-pinned scripts/teleport-monster-traps.test.mjs test verifies the LEVEL_TELEP branch uses injected rn2 bounds [5,3], migrates to the selected next level, marks the trap seen, emits the C disappearance message, and sets confusion when the monster lacks teleport control.

After the RNG-routing fix, bounded exact replay run-XXamzL of the unchanged admitted recording matches all 415 screens, 2480 RNG calls and 415 cursor positions with no replay error. Focused test run-RDFZKp passes 11/11 tests; npm run lint exits 0.
